learn.canDo: Explain how a container is told to stop, and set up exec form, a SIGTERM handler, an init and a grace period so shutdown is clean.
learn.why: Dropped requests on every deploy usually come from a signal that never arrives. It is a quick, concrete win.
learn.keyIdea: A handler only runs in the process that gets the signal.

learn.canDo: Explain how the OOM killer chooses, contain a leak with limits, and protect the database.
learn.why: Exit code 137 is among the most common production mysteries. Knowing who the kernel kills and why is the answer.
learn.keyIdea: The kernel knows who is big, not who is at fault.

learn.canDo: Work out descriptors per connection, size the limit where the process is launched, and close what you open.
learn.why: 'Too many open files' is a classic limit that looks like a capacity problem. The fix is arithmetic and discipline.
learn.keyIdea: A bigger limit buys time. Only closing the file stops the leak.

learn.canDo: Write a unit that restarts transient failures quickly, stops retrying hopeless ones, and fails visibly.
learn.why: Every host runs a supervisor. Restart policy is part of the availability number.
learn.keyIdea: Heal what can heal. Give up loudly on what can't.

learn.canDo: Find the cause of a vanished service with journalctl and the kernel log, and keep evidence that survives a reboot.
learn.why: The first minutes of an incident decide how well you can investigate it. Logs that survive are what make that possible.
learn.keyIdea: Logs outlive the machine that wrote them.

learn.canDo: Compare average CPU use with a baseline, predict a throttle, and decide between standard, unlimited and fixed-performance instances.
learn.why: Burstable instances are everywhere, and their throttle looks like an idle machine. Knowing the cliff saves a long debugging session.
learn.keyIdea: A pinned low number is a throttle, not a rest.

chapter.story: A server that worked in testing starts dying at night, and the team has to learn what the operating system is doing.
outcomes: Explain signals, memory limits and descriptor limits
Write a restart policy that heals without looping
Keep evidence that survives a reboot
Recognise a CPU throttle on a burstable instance
chapter.why: Production problems are usually the operating system doing what it was designed to do. Knowing the defaults is half of every diagnosis.
chapter.payoff: In an interview you can walk through why a process died. At work you will read a kernel log and know what you are looking at.
